newsitem.title: CHINA: Dresdner opens Beijing branch, plans fund.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner opens Beijing branch, plans fund.

text.p: Germany's Dresdner Bank AG opened a branch in Beijing on Friday and company officials said they were applying to start a fund management joint venture with a Chinese securities firm.

Dresdner, the first European bank to open a full branch in Beijing, would make the new office the bank's headquarters for its China operations, Jurgen Sarrazin, chairman of the bank's board of managing directors, told a news briefing.
The bank's China business had been coordinated out of its Hong Kong office.
Sarrazin said the fund management joint venture would be set up with a leading Chinese securities firm, though he declined to name the potential partner.
"We are just now preparing all our documentation which we have to file with the authorities and we are quite sure that we will receive a favourable reaction to it," he said.

The bank's Shanghai branch expected to receive a licence in the near future to conduct business in the local yuan currency, he said, adding he foresaw the many restrictions on such business eventually being lifted.
China had previously restricted all foreign banks to foreign currency business but it has begun allowing them to take deposits and extend loans in limited volumes of local currency.
Foreign banks handling yuan business must open a branch in Shanghai's Pudong area and face quotas on the size of loans they can extend.
"We expect that these restrictions that so far exist... will be lifted soon and that permission might be extended to other financial centres," he said without elaborating.
Dresdner has full branches in Shanghai and Shenzhen near Hong Kong, a representative office in the southern city of Guangzhou, and a stake in a Chinese leasing firm.
